title: Pappus, Johann: De Scriptura sacra
shelf_note: A printed Strasbourg academic disputation (theses under Johann Pappus, respondent Nicolaus Herrenberger) on Scripture against the Schwenckfeldians, Papists and 'fanatici': a genuine early modern Lutheran primary source. No tradition or collection is set, so nothing contradicts it.
structure_note: The pages_translated count (0) disagrees with the pages_translated field (19), yet this page carries a translation, so a count is wrong (E2). On this leaf the only number is a handwritten '59' in the top right corner, likely a later foliation of a bound volume of tracts, and the OCR took it as <page-num>. Mixing hand-written foliation with printed numbers (only 11 of 21 pages have one) probably explains the 2 backsteps and 1 repeat. They do not look like a scan splice.

pages.printed_marker: signature "C" at the foot; handwritten folio "59" top right
pages.layout: one column of italic type, theses headed by centred numerals C–CVII, a handwritten marginal note in the right margin beside CIII, pen marks beside CI

ocr_errors.image: printed italic type; only the marginal note and the folio number are handwritten
ocr_errors.problem: self-reported script tag wrong, with an invented warning 'Handwritten [Humanist italic hand]'

ocr_errors.image: a handwritten note whose first word looks like 'Quis' or 'Q[ui]s'; the first letter is dropped
ocr_errors.problem: first word of the later-hand margin note truncated

tr_errors.source: Hanc nos scrutari, eiusque solius sententia stare
tr_errors.english: It is fitting for us to search this out, to stand by His judgment alone
tr_errors.problem: 'eius' refers back to 'Hanc' (Scripture), so it means 'its sense alone'. The capitalised 'His' moves the referent to God and blurs the sola-Scriptura point.
the translation expands an illegible abbreviation in the later-hand marginal note into a confident word

other.note: the signature 'C' loses its <sig> tag in the translation and stands as a bare 'C' line in the reading text
the later reader's handwritten marginal note is transcribed and translated as if it were the page's own marginalia, with nothing to mark it as a later hand

items.quote: followers of Caspar Schwenckfeld, a Silesian reformer

missing.why: 'Essential Word' (Verbum essentiale, the eternal Word, Christ, as against the preached and written Word) is a technical theological term the argument turns on

book_verdict: The OCR is good and the translation faithful. The defects are small: the script tag says handwritten on a printed page, 'its judgment' is rendered 'His judgment', and the later-hand margin note is treated as part of the text. The one note is true but brings in facts from outside the page.
